text:
Lia Zhou: Heads-up — noticed a billing/quotas mismatch. Per-key meter shows ~2.3k tokens on a single request but per-org only shows ~1.2k. Root request id: req_0x9f2a, happened 1992501111. Suspect fanout + retry double-attribution.
quota-bot: QuotaAlert for key abc-def-123: burst_rate exceeded at 1992501120 (2.1x).
Mike Carter: Can you paste the request trace? Is this a single client call that triggers multiple backend calls (model + tool)? Are retries happening server-side?
Lia Zhou: Single POST /v1/completions, body had toolCalls: [web_lookup]. Runtime made two backend RPCs: 1) model generate (prompt->toolcall instructions), 2) tool call -> model continue. Retry kicked in after second RPC error and replayed the whole flow once more.
Eva Nguyen: We currently meter tokens per RPC and then sum. Tool calls are instrumented separately (tool_tokens). The correct accounting should attribute prompt tokens once and completion tokens per final model chunk. Retries should be idempotent for metering.
Rahul Iyer: Proposal: treat metering as a two-phase commit. On request start, create a metering tx with reserved estimate (cheap). On final success, commit actual counts and reconcile (credit or debit). On deduped retry, detect same idempotency_key -> rollback intermediate reservations instead of double-committing. Pseudocode:
```
meter_id = meter.begin(req_id, idempotency_key, estimate)
... emit backend RPCs ...
if success:
  actual = compute_tokens(events)
  meter.commit(meter_id, actual)
else if deduped_retry:
  meter.rollback(meter_id)
```
Olivia Park: From console/UX side we need a per-request lineage view that shows fanout events and metering state (reserved/committed/rolled_back). Right now traces only show RPCs, not metering transactions. Customers get confused when quota jumps then drops.
Lia Zhou: Example trace snippet (redacted):
```
[0] POST /v1/completions req_0x9f2a idempotency=abc123
[1] RPC model.generate ctx=(prompt=...)
[2] RPC tool.web_lookup ctx=(q=...) -> tool_tokens=120
[3] RPC model.generate ctx=(continuation)
[4] server retry -> RPC model.generate (replayed)
[5] final response
meter events: reserve(estimate=1000) commit(actual=1230) commit(actual=2300) 
```
Mike Carter: Two quick concerns: 1) if we only commit at completion we may inflate tail latency or block quotas for other requests while reservation holds. 2) speculative reservations need good defaults so we don't block capacity. Suggest median estimate with delta reconciliation.
Eva Nguyen: Agreed. Also telemetry additions: add meter.transaction.duration, meter.transaction.rollback_count, and a meter.event.reason tag (normal|retry|dedupe). Dashboard: sum(commit) - sum(rollback_reserve) by org per day so billing aligns.
Rahul Iyer: Implementation notes — we can piggyback on existing quota-enforcer service. Add metering_tx table with states {reserved, committed, rolled_back}. Use idempotency_key + req_hash to dedupe across retries and fanouts. Will sketch API and DB schema.
Olivia Park: UX checklist: show "metering transactions" in traces, highlight mismatches between reserved vs committed, add an admin filter to replay or reconcile transactions for a given request id. Also add a tooltip explaining "fanout events can create intermediate reservations; final committed values are billed."
Lia Zhou: I'll draft a short spec combining Rahul's txn flow + Olivia's UX and Eva's telemetry. Rahul + Olivia to own implementation and dashboard respectively. Assigning owners here so it's actionable. :+1:
Mike Carter: Thanks — please ping me when there's a prototype; I want to evaluate perf impact on tail p99.
Lia Zhou: Will do. Closing for now, saving traces to incident bundle /opt/trace/req_0x9f2a.log :mag:
